title: Clinical Mastery: Sickle Cell Retinopathy (SCR)
summary: Sickle cell retinopathy represents a spectrum of vaso-occlusive ocular manifestations stemming from hemoglobinopathies. Understanding the transition from non-proliferative to proliferative stages is critical for preventing irreversible vision loss through timely peripheral retinal ischemia management.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Sickle cell retinopathy (SCR) comprises ocular changes associated with HbSS (Sickle Cell Anemia), HbSC, and HbS-thalassemia. Pathophysiology is driven by the polymerization of deoxygenated HbS, leading to erythrocyte rigidity, vascular stasis, and microvascular occlusion. Chronic ischemia triggers an upregulation of VEGF, promoting neovascularization.

sections.title: Red Flags for Intervention
content: Presence of Goldberg Stage III Neovascularization (Sea Fans)
Any evidence of fresh vitreous hemorrhage
Symptoms of flashes or floaters indicating retinal traction
Peripheral retinal edema indicating active ischemia
History of hyphema in the context of sickle trait/disease

rows: Salmon patch hemorrhages, Black sunbursts, Silver wire vessels
Sea fan neovascularization at the junction of perfused/non-perfused retina
Iris atrophy, hyphema (often associated with increased IOP)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Dilated fundus examination with indirect ophthalmoscopy and scleral depression (Gold Standard).
Step 2: Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) to identify peripheral non-perfusion and early sea fans.
Step 3: OCT Macula to rule out ischemia and epiretinal membranes.
Step 4: B-Scan Ultrasonography if media is opaque (e.g., dense vitreal hemorrhage) to rule out RD.

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Observation: Routine monitoring for quiescent sea fans (auto-infarction is possible).
Laser Photocoagulation: Feeder vessel treatment or scatter photocoagulation of ischemic areas for active sea fans.
Anti-VEGF: Off-label use for pre-vitrectomy to reduce intraoperative bleeding.
Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV): Indicated for non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage or tractional RD.
Anterior Chamber Irrigation: Immediate washout for traumatic hyphema with elevated IOP.

content.explanation: B: Black sunbursts (RPE hyperplasia), A: Arteriolar occlusion, S: Sea fans (neovasc), S: Salmon patch (intraretinal hemorrhage).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: HbSC genotype has the highest risk of PDR due to higher blood viscosity.
Always perform systemic screening; patients with PDR should have their hemoglobin status confirmed.
Avoid carbonic anhydrase inhibitors in acute hyphema/increased IOP (can shift pH and induce sickling).
Sea fans are usually located in the temporal periphery.
